title: Kenyan Sugar-Coated Groundnuts
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Sugar-Coated Groundnuts — roasted groundnuts coated in a crispy white sugar shell with cardamom and vanilla. The sweet counterpart to the classic salted roasted groundnut — equally beloved and completely addictive.
longDesc: Sugar-coated groundnuts are the celebration version of Kenya's favourite snack — sold at weddings, school prize-givings, market stalls, and festive gatherings. The groundnuts are coated in a white sugar shell that cracks satisfyingly when bitten, revealing the roasted nut within. The addition of cardamom gives them a distinctly Kenyan aromatic character.
ingredients: 2 cups roasted groundnuts — skins on or removed
steps: Combine sugar and water in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Stir until sugar dissolves. Stop stirring and bring to a boil.
Cook without stirring until the syrup reaches 115°C (soft ball stage) — about 8—10 minutes.
Add groundnuts, cardamom, vanilla, and salt. Stir vigorously.
Keep stirring over medium-low heat as the sugar begins to crystallise around the nuts — it will turn white and grainy.
Continue stirring until all nuts are coated in dry, white sugar crystals — about 3—5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Pour onto a greased tray.
Quickly separate any clumps with a fork.
chefTips: The crystallisation stage (when the syrup goes white and grainy) is expected and correct — keep stirring through it.
Once the sugar crystallises, the nuts dry quickly — work fast to separate them.
For a brown-sugar caramelised version: cook the syrup to 130°C instead of 115°C.
commonMistakes: Stopping stirring when the sugar goes grainy — the nuts clump permanently.
Syrup too hot — the sugar caramelises instead of forming the white crystal coating.
cookingScience: At 115°C, the sugar solution is supersaturated. When agitated (stirring), it crystallises rapidly — the stirring provides nucleation points for crystal formation, coating each nut in a thick layer of fine sugar crystals rather than a glassy caramel.
sustainabilityTips: Buy from local Kenyan groundnut farmers.
storage: Airtight container for up to 3 weeks.
healthBenefits: Groundnuts provide protein and healthy fats.
Best enjoyed as a celebration treat.
culturalNote: Sugar-coated groundnuts are one of the most cherished celebration sweets in Kenya — bags of karanga za sukari appear at weddings, school events, and festive gatherings as tokens of sweetness shared with guests.
